pr_title: Fix find by with postgres point
pr_body:
### Summary

Closes #42268 

The bug trying to be fixed here is the one that happens when we try to do `find_by` with a Postgres point.
As equality in Postgres with points is done with `~=` instead of `=` I rewrote the methods involved with the proper syntax.

### Other Information
 - Even though the test passes, **I'm still not sure if this is the right solution** or if I'm missing any scenarios. Any kind of feedback is more than welcome
 - I based my solution on the hint @ghiculescu left (thanks so much 😄 )
pr_comments: @martinjaimem It's great you were able to turn this into a patch, I'm still not sure though if this is the right approach so I will defer until we get some more feedback 🙏

I spent some time looking at `Point` code and prepared alternative implementation using more high-level API.

https://github.com/rails/rails/compare/main...simi:point-eq-operator?expand=1

It is not 100% done and not covered by tests where possible, but all tests from this PR are passing. It could be inspiration for alternative approach. It supports also negative (`WHERE NOT`) version. On the other side it is touching various places of code only useful for PostgreSQL adapter. It could be most likely little restructured. Also I'm not sure what is going to happen when another adapter (like MySQL) is going to somehow use `point` even it is not supported.

This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity. It will be closed if no further activity occurs.
Thank you for your contributions.

Since this PR was closed, would it be worth making a PR with @simi's alternative approach? Not an expert on ActiveRecord internals but the [diff](https://github.com/rails/rails/compare/main...simi:point-eq-operator) looks pretty clean.

issue_context.title: Postgres + ActiveRecord::Point uses invalid equal operator (= instead of ~=) on find_or_create_by()
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
```ruby
require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  # Activate the gem you are reporting the issue against.
  gem "activerecord", "6.1.3.2"
  gem "pg"
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "postgresql", database: "test-db")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :addresses, force: true do |t|
    t.point :coordinates
  end
end

class Address < ActiveRecord::Base
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_nested_saving
    address = Address.find_or_create_by!({ coordinates: ActiveRecord::Point.new(0, 0) })

    assert address
  end
end

```

### Expected behavior
I would expect it to use the correct `~=` operator for comparison when a `ActiveRecord::Point` type is provided (explicitly or otherwise). 

### Actual behavior
It attempts to use the `=` operator for equality comparison which is invalid (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/13/functions-geometry.html)

### System configuration
**Rails version**: Rails 6.1.3.2
**Ruby version**: ruby 3.0.1p64 (2021-04-05 revision 0fb782ee38) [x86_64-darwin20]
comments:
I've been playing around with this. Haven't quite got it working but I think(?) I'm on the right track. Happy for someone else to run with it though.

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activerecord/lib/arel/visitors/postgresql.rb

```ruby
        def visit_Arel_Nodes_HomogeneousIn(o, collector)
          if o.type == :in && o.attribute.type_caster.is_a?(ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PostgreSQL::OID::Point)
            collector.preparable = false

            collector << quote_table_name(o.table_name) << "." << quote_column_name(o.column_name) << " ~= "

            values = o.casted_values
            if values.empty?
              collector << @connection.quote(nil)
            else
              collector << "'(#{values.join(', ')})'"
            end

            collector
          else
            super
          end
        end

        def visit_Arel_Nodes_Equality(o, collector)
          if o.left.type_caster.is_a?(ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PostgreSQL::OID::Point)
            values = o.casted_values
            collector << " =~ " << "'(#{values.join(', ')})'"
            visit right, collector
          else
            super
          end
        end
```

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activerecord/test/cases/adapters/postgresql/geometric_test.rb

```ruby
  def test_find_by
    point = PostgresqlPoint.create! x: [10, 25.2]

    assert_equal point, PostgresqlPoint.find_by(x: [10, 25.2]) # passing
    assert_equal point, PostgresqlPoint.where(x: [10, 25.2]).first # passing

    assert_equal point, PostgresqlPoint.find_by(x: ActiveRecord::Point.new(10, 25.2)) # not passing yet
  end
```

I can repro the issue with the latest version of ActiveRecord.
